scope: Implemented quiet-interval CPU execution and isolated cold-rollback extraction, evaluated original-ROM fixed workloads, then restored the original production core. No new CPU performance optimization is shipped.

decision.v3: withdrawn: default-Chrome HP48gII 7*8 crosses the existing >10% median elapsed and at-least-three-of-four-slower rollback threshold; aggregate Chrome elapsed also increases.
decision.v4: withdrawn: Chrome sum of the six scene medians does not decrease. The near-zero difference does not establish a stable regression; it fails the predeclared selection condition.
decision.v4_rule_declared_before_sampling: Require every correctness comparison to pass; require sum(scene median candidate Chrome ms) < sum(scene median baseline Chrome ms); reject if any Chrome scene has median(candidate)/median(baseline)-1 > 0.10 and at least 3 of 4 paired candidate samples are slower. Node is auxiliary, published unchanged.

final_release.name_section_difference: Only the module output name in the custom name section differs: baseline-production.wasm versus orchard.wasm. The 12-byte difference has no executable effect.

v1.change: bounded quiet-interval continuation for ordinary ARM ALU, branch and failed-condition instructions; no later instruction prefetched

v2.change: also continue after successful ARM word/byte single transfers; MMIO clears the quiet interval and abort/diagnostic paths return

v3.change: v2 plus noinline cold CPU transaction and inlined hot step; exact production source order

reconstruction_patch.scope: Core source differences only, relative to the restored r17 baseline.
reconstruction_patch.status: Withdrawn research candidate; retained for review and reproducibility only. Not enabled in production.

v4.change: only noinline cold CPU transaction extracted; original void cpu_step, machine loop, headers and profiling tool restored

reconstruction_patch.scope: Core source differences only, relative to the restored r17 baseline.
reconstruction_patch.status: Withdrawn research candidate; retained for review and reproducibility only. Not enabled in production.

method.timing_scope: Fixed guest work from saved original-ROM sessions through the full expected result and completed contact releases. This is host throughput, not production UI input-to-display latency or physical-calculator timing.
method.aggregation: Per scene median(baseline)/median(candidate); aggregate sum(scene baseline medians)/sum(scene candidate medians). Node and Chrome remain separate.
method.paired_estimator: median(candidate_i/baseline_i)-1, retained alongside ratio-of-medians elapsed change.
method.fixture_migration: Existing v1 sessions were imported and exported through the baseline core to v2. Browser comparisons then used identical wire versions and compared every final checkpoint byte.
method.standalone_multiplication: Both 7*8 fixtures start from HOME rather than after 1+1, so complete LCD hashes include their own distinct screen history.

experiments.isolation_note: Exploratory run without coordinated isolation; other team original-ROM probes overlapped this phase. Not used to claim a final speedup.

complete_original_report.checkpoint_comparison: Validate each wire checksum and exact schema layout, then migrate v1 to v2 by inserting only the documented 52-byte SDI reset state. Compare every canonical byte, including SDI, CPU, peripheral state, RAM and boot SRAM. Raw wire hashes are retained separately.
complete_original_report.process_cpu_measurement: process.cpuUsage user plus system time; may include V8 background work. exec_argv records engine switches. --no-liftoff requests optimizing WASM compilation up front for a separate steady-state experiment; default-engine browser measurements are still required.
complete_original_report.measurement: Node/V8 execution from exact private scene checkpoints to the baseline first full LCD result, including all key releases and their final gap. Each variant executes the complete workload twice before alternating timed replays; the first baseline replay locates the result. Loading, explicit WASM compilation, restore, LCD sampling and final checkpoint hashing are outside timed intervals. JS key scheduling, UART draining and incremental UART hashing are included. This is host execution throughput, not browser latency or real-calculator calibration.

complete_original_report.measurement: Two complete warmups per variant, then four alternating AB/BA timed replays per scene. Production WASM executes in a dedicated WebWorker under default Chrome with no V8 flags. Loading, explicit compilation, restore, LCD inspection and hashes are outside timing. Key scheduling and UART draining/byte capture are inside; WebCrypto UART hashing is outside. No Worker pacing, UI input, snapshot delivery or canvas rendering is timed.

final_asan_ubsan.checkpoint_guard_followup: Only checkpoint-regression was rebuilt and rerun after the test-size guard correction; other test sources and core binaries were unchanged.

Reject invalid checkpoint size before test offset arithmetic, and retain the model RAM length in a local variable.
